question: Will Flávio Bolsonaro finish in second place in the first round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election?
resolution_criteria:
A presidential election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 4, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the listed candidate who receives the second-most valid votes in the first round of this election.

The named candidates will be primarily ranked by the number of valid votes received in the specified election. If two or more candidates are tied on valid votes, ties will be broken by alphabetical order of the candidates' last names. This market will resolve to the candidate that occupies the second-highest finishing position after applying this ranking.

If the result of this election isn't known definitively by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).
research:
# Research report 1 of 2

I couldn't find any poll from before the cutoff showing a candidate other than Lula or Flávio Bolsonaro within about 20 points of second place. The main way Flávio misses second is by beating Lula and finishing first. Polls up to the cutoff had Lula ahead by about 6 to 10 points. Three page fetches (the TSE source, a full Wikipedia polling table and an Orrery market page) were refused by the proxy, so most of what follows comes from search summaries of the articles. I left out everything dated after 2026-09-22, including a Datafolha poll released on 23 September.

## 1. Resolution source
- The deciding source is the Superior Electoral Court's (TSE) official first-round count, ranked by valid votes, with credible reporting as the first check. The first round is scheduled for 2026-10-04.
- I could not get a live reading or date from the TSE page because the fetch was refused. As of the 2026-09-22 cutoff, no results existed.
- Flávio finishes second only if Lula beats him and no third candidate passes him.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settled the question before the cutoff.
- Every major pollster's most recent national poll before the cutoff had Flávio second behind Lula. In those polls the third-place candidate was 20 or more points below him.
- One outlier (Veritá, published 2026-04, fieldwork 13 March to 4 April) had Flávio first with 35.9% to Lula's 33.2%. [CNN Brasil](https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/eleicoes/verita-flavio-tem-359-e-lula-332-no-1o-turno/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-10: PoderData had Augusto Cury (Avante) at 10%, Renan Santos (Missão) at 3%, Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) at 2% and Romeu Zema (Novo) at 1%. It was the first time Cury reached double digits with that pollster. [Gazeta do Povo](https://www.gazetadopovo.com.br/eleicoes/2026/pesquisa-eleitoral-2026/augusto-cury-primeiro-candidato-que-ultrapassou-10-intencoes-de-voto-alem-de-flavio-lula/)
- 2026-09-14: This was the TSE deadline to approve or block presidential candidacies. Renan Santos's candidacy was the subject of a suspension controversy. [Gazeta do Povo](https://www.gazetadopovo.com.br/eleicoes/2026/ascensao-de-cury-e-posicao-antissistema-de-renan-santos-isolam-ex-governadores/)
- 2026-09-03: Datafolha (fieldwork 1 to 3 September, 2,002 interviews, ±2 points): first round Lula 38%, Flávio 32%; second round Lula 46%, Flávio 44%. [Gazeta do Povo](https://www.gazetadopovo.com.br/eleicoes/2026/pesquisa-eleitoral-2026/datafolha-presidente-setembro-2026/)
- About 2026-09-02: Quaest had Lula 37%, Flávio 30% and Cury 10% in the first round, with a 42% to 41% tie in the second round. [Gazeta do Povo](https://www.gazetadopovo.com.br/eleicoes/2026/pesquisa-eleitoral-2026/quaest-presidente-setembro-2026/)
- 2026-08-31: Nexus/BTG had Lula 37%, Flávio 31% and Cury 11%. [Gazeta do Povo](https://www.gazetadopovo.com.br/eleicoes/2026/pesquisa-eleitoral-2026/pesquisas-que-confirmam-avanco-augusto-cury/)
- Late August (fieldwork 25 to 30 August): AtlasIntel had Lula 43.4% and Flávio 33.7% in the first round, with Cury around 7.8% and Renan Santos around 7.6%. [Gazeta do Povo](https://www.gazetadopovo.com.br/eleicoes/2026/pesquisa-eleitoral-2026/atlasintel-presidente-agosto-2026/)
- About 2026-06-08: Quaest had Lula 39% and Flávio 29%. The Perseu Abramo Foundation (linked to Lula's party, the PT) blamed Flávio's drop on leaked audio recordings. [FPA](https://fpabramo.org.br/lula-flavio-bolsonaro-primeiro-turno-pesquisa-quaest/)
- 2026-03: Datafolha had a second-round tie, Lula 46% and Flávio 43%. Ratinho Júnior dropped out on 23 March. [Yahoo/Reuters](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/flavio-bolsonaro-draws-even-lula-161733328.html), [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Social_Democratic_Party_presidential_selection)

## 4. Base rates
- In Brazil's two-round elections from 1989 to 2022, the two leaders in the final polls have almost always been the top two in the first round. The order has usually matched the polls, though 2022 is an exception to watch: Lula led by about 14 points in Datafolha's final poll but won by about 5. That was from my own background knowledge; I did not verify it with a search here.
- Polls before the cutoff consistently put Lula ahead of Flávio in the first round, from about 6 points (Datafolha, early September) to about 10 points (AtlasIntel, late August). The gap was 9 to 13 points in January and 10 points in June, so it narrowed over the year.
- The closest third-place candidate was Cury at 7.8% to 11%, about 20 points behind Flávio.

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-04-02: Lines.com reported Polymarket's "YES" price for Flávio in second at about 60%, but its headline cited 72%, so the source contradicts itself. [Lines](https://www.lines.com/prediction-markets/elections/brazil-presidential-election-first-round-2nd-place)
- About 2026-04-30: Kalshi priced Lula for second at about 26¢, against about 19¢ on Polymarket. [SimpleFunctions](https://simplefunctions.dev/api/public/market/KXBRPRESIDENT2-BRPRES26-2-LSIL)
- 2026-05-18: Orrery showed Polymarket at about 62% for Flávio in second. [Orrery](https://www.orrery.me/markets/will-flvio-bolsonaro-finish-in-second-place-in-the-first-round-of-the-2026-brazilian-presidential-election)
- Undated: Polyguana showed Zema's second-place contract at about 96¢ "No", and Caiado's and Geraldo Alckmin's also strongly "No". [Polyguana](https://polyguana.com/es/events/brazil-presidential-election-first-round-2nd-place)
- I could not find a Polymarket or Kalshi price from September 2026.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- More Datafolha, Quaest and AtlasIntel polls before 4 October, including the final ones.
- TV debates in the last weeks of the campaign.
- Possible tactical voting on the right moving Cury's or Renan Santos's supporters to Flávio, which could narrow or reverse the gap with Lula.
- The vote itself on 2026-10-04, with TSE results expected that night.

# Research report 2 of 2 (written independently)

I couldn't open any pages directly because the proxy refused every fetch (Wikipedia, Gazeta do Povo, CNN Brasil, the market aggregators). Everything below comes from search-result snippets, so check the key numbers before relying on them. Some search results also included material dated after 2026-09-22. I ignored all of it.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on the official first-round results from the TSE (dadosabertos.tse.jus.br) or a consensus of credible reporting. The first round is on 2026-10-04. As of 2026-09-22 no votes have been cast, so the TSE has no results to show. I could not fetch the TSE site.
- The rule only counts the listed candidate in second place by valid votes. Flávio does not resolve "Yes" if he finishes first or third.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. In every September poll I found, Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) is second behind Lula (PT), and he leads the third-placed candidate, Augusto Cury, by more than 20 points. So the realistic way this fails is Flávio finishing **first**, not falling to third. The Lula-Flávio gap is about 2 to 8 points, depending on the poll.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- Mid-Sept 2026 (exact dates unconfirmed): the Portuguese Wikipedia poll table lists Datafolha (fieldwork Sept 15-16), Quaest (Sept 17-20) and AtlasIntel (Sept 11-16). The snippet was garbled. Read as Lula vs Flávio, the figures are roughly 44-44, 39-35 and 45.6-37.8, but the columns could not be confirmed. [pt.wikipedia](https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pesquisas_de_opini%C3%A3o_para_a_elei%C3%A7%C3%A3o_presidencial_no_Brasil_em_2026)
- Sept 2026 (date unconfirmed): an AtlasIntel first-round poll had Lula 46.3% and Flávio 43.9%. [Gazeta do Povo](https://www.gazetadopovo.com.br/eleicoes/2026/pesquisa-eleitoral-2026/atlasintel-presidente-setembro-2026-3/)
- ~2026-09-02: Quaest, its first poll of the official campaign: Lula 37%, Flávio 30%, Cury 10%, Renan Santos 3%; Caiado, Zema and Marçal 1% each. Runoff: Lula 42%, Flávio 41%. [Gazeta do Povo](https://www.gazetadopovo.com.br/eleicoes/2026/pesquisa-eleitoral-2026/quaest-presidente-setembro-2026/)
- 2026-09-01 to 03 (fieldwork): Datafolha: Lula 38%, Flávio 33%, Cury 8%, Caiado 4%, Renan Santos 3%. [CNN Brasil](https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/eleicoes/datafolha-no-1o-turno-lula-tem-38-flavio-33-e-cury-8/)
- ~2026-08-31 / 09-01: Real Time Big Data had Lula 38, Flávio 30, Cury 11. BTG/Nexus had 39/33/11. AtlasIntel/Bloomberg had 43.4/33.7/7.8. [Congresso em Foco](https://www.congressoemfoco.com.br/noticia/121834/augusto-cury-cresce-e-aparece-em-3-na-pesquisa-real-time-big-data)
- 2026-03: Datafolha had a runoff technical tie, Lula 46 to Flávio 43, with Lula leading every first-round scenario. [Yahoo/Reuters](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/flavio-bolsonaro-draws-even-lula-161733328.html)
- 2025-12-06: Flávio launched his candidacy with his father's endorsement. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/12/6/flavio-bolsonaro-enters-brazils-2026-presidential-race-with-fathers-nod)

## 4. Base rates
- Since 2006, every Brazilian first round has been a two-way contest, with third place far behind. That fits the current polls, where third place is around 10%.
- Main risk to "Yes": a polling error on the first-place margin.
  - In 2022, final polls had Lula ahead by a wide margin (Datafolha about 14 points among valid votes). The result was Lula 48.4%, Bolsonaro 43.2%: the right-wing candidate beat his polls by several points.
  - In 2018, Jair Bolsonaro came first in round one.
  - This is from my background knowledge, not a source I fetched.
- In the polls above, the Lula-Flávio gap ranges from about 0 to 8 points across pollsters, with AtlasIntel and Datafolha tighter in mid-September. A gap of this size is within a 2022-sized polling error.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket "Flávio Bolsonaro 2nd in first round":
  - About 70% in April 2026 (one April 2 listing showed $0.60, conflicting with a 72% figure in the same article's header). [Lines](https://www.lines.com/prediction-markets/elections/brazil-presidential-election-first-round-2nd-place)
  - About 62% on 2026-05-18. [Orrery](https://www.orrery.me/markets/will-flvio-bolsonaro-finish-in-second-place-in-the-first-round-of-the-2026-brazilian-presidential-election)
- Kalshi equivalent (KXBRPRESIDENT2): about 51 on 2026-05-28. [SimpleFunctions](https://simplefunctions.dev/api/public/market/KXBRPRESIDENT2-BRPRES26-2-FBOL)
- A snippet from a September 2026 analysis said Flávio's probability of finishing second fell 13 points while Lula's rose 15, which suggests the market moved toward Flávio finishing first. I could not see the date or the source. [Octagon](https://www.octagonai.co/markets/politics/brazil/brazil-presidential-election-first-round-2nd-place/)
- I could not find a Polymarket or Kalshi price dated close to 2026-09-22.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Final Datafolha, Quaest and AtlasIntel polls are expected in late September and early October. I found nothing dated after the cutoff that I could use.
- The final TV debates are customarily held in the days before the vote (traditionally TV Globo around Oct 1-2). I did not confirm the 2026 schedule.
- First round: 2026-10-04, with the TSE count the same night. A runoff is expected if no one gets more than 50% of valid votes.
- Watch tactical voting: Cury's and Caiado's voters moving to Flávio could push him into first.

- Runoff polls are essentially tied (Quaest 42 to 41, Datafolha 46 to 44 in early September).
  - One undated September AtlasIntel poll reportedly had Lula 46.3, Flávio 43.9 in the first round.
  - Right-wing candidates beat their polls in 2018 and 2022.
  - Voters for Cury, Caiado, Zema and Renan Santos (about 15% combined) could move tactically to Flávio.
  - An undated September snippet says the market probability of Flávio in second fell 13 points while Lula in second rose 15.

(e) Scenarios:
- **No:** polls understate Flávio by 4 to 6 points on the margin as in 2022, and late consolidation of the right pushes him narrowly ahead of Lula, for example 44 to 43 in valid votes, so he finishes first.
- **Yes:** polls are roughly right or err modestly, Lula also gains from tactical voting on the left, and he finishes first by 3 to 6 points with Flávio a clear second.

(f) From base rate to final: I take a Lula lead of about 5.5 points and subtract about 2 points for the historical bias against the right, leaving an effective lead of about 3.5. With a standard deviation of about 6 points on the margin error, that gives roughly a 28 to 33% chance that Flávio finishes first. A third-place finish adds about 1%. The narrowing trend and the reported market move toward Flávio finishing first pull me a few points below the 70% base rate. Earlier market prices (about 62% on Polymarket and 51% on Kalshi in May) are stale, but they are consistent with a low-60s estimate.

Probability: 63%
